- Raspberry Pi 5 + power supply + SD card
- ADALM-MMSC board (contains the AD4080 and a pre-programmed MAX32666FTHR microcontroller running the IIO server)
- ADALM2000 board (Multi-function USB instrument)
- Two micro-USB cables (one for the ADALM2000, one for the ADALM-MMSC)
- Jumper wires: the ADA

The ADALM-MMSC is powered and read over its USB connection, so no firmware programming or additional power supply is needed; the board ships with the IIO server firmware already loaded. (Firmware upgrade instructions are in the ADALM-MMSC documentation.)

Create the environment:

```default
python3 -m venv --system-site-packages .venv
```

Genalyzer is a C library with Python bindings. It isn’t packaged for this image, so we compile version v0.1.7 from source.

Download the source:

```default
git clone --branch v0.1.7 --depth 1 https://github.com/analogdevicesinc/genalyzer /tmp/genalyzer
```

Communication with the various data converter sources and sinks is done through the Industrial I/O (IIO) framework. This framework is used for communicating with devices that are in some sense an ADC or DAC, and is the backbone of many of the tools we will use in this workshop. An important concept

Scopy is a GUI application that provides the test instrument interfaces to the ADALM2000, as well as custom instruments for other hardware, such as the AD-SWIOT1L-SL Software-configurable Analog and Digital I/O with 10BASE-T1L. Most examples in this workshop are Python scripts. Thonny is a Python IDE and will allow you to edit and run them easily. In the setup, Thonny was installed in the workshop’s Python virtual environment, which has all the required packages. Open a terminal and run:

```default
thonny
```

The ADALM-MMSC does not have to deliver all 40 MSPS. Its AD4080 includes a digital filter that decimates the data to a lower rate, and the simplest option is the sinc1 filter. It is cheap and fast, but not a brick-wall filter: signals above the new, lower Nyquist frequency are only attenuated, and w

A seismic signal is slow, only a few hertz, while the AD4080 samples at 40 MSPS, so the ADALM-MMSC’s digital filter does the work of bringing the data rate down to something suitable.
